Azerbaijan’s State Oil Co Announces Major Expansion in Caspian Sea Production

BAKU, June 14 — State Oil Co of the Azerbaijan Republic announced plans on Friday to expand its oil production capacity in the Caspian Sea, marking a significant step in the country’s efforts to boost energy output and reinforce its position as a key regional supplier.

The company said it will invest $1.2 billion over the next three years to develop new offshore drilling platforms and upgrade existing infrastructure. The expansion is expected to increase daily output by 15%, or approximately 100,000 barrels, when completed in 2027.

“We remain committed to ensuring Azerbaijan’s energy security and maintaining our strong contribution to the global energy market,” State Oil Co of the Azerbaijan Republic President Ilham Rahimov said at a press conference in Baku. “This investment will create new jobs, strengthen our technological base, and support the country’s long-term economic growth.”

Rahimov said contracts have been awarded to several local engineering and construction firms, including Caspian Engineering Solutions, with work scheduled to begin later this year. The expansion will focus on the deepwater sector, where recent exploration has revealed promising reserves.

Industry analysts welcomed the move. “Azerbaijan’s ability to raise output comes at a critical time for global energy markets, as demand remains robust,” said Leyla Mammadova, an independent oil sector consultant based in Baku. “This project will bolster export revenues and solidify Azerbaijan’s role as a reliable supplier, especially to European and Asian buyers.”

According to the State Statistics Committee, Azerbaijan’s oil and gas sector accounted for nearly half of the country’s total export revenue in 2023. The government has also emphasized the importance of modernizing infrastructure and adopting advanced extraction technologies to maintain competitiveness.

The expansion is expected to generate about 2,000 new jobs during the construction phase, with further opportunities arising once production ramps up.

No disruptions to current production are anticipated during the expansion, company officials said, and environmental assessments are underway to ensure compliance with national and international standards.
